title: Docker & Docker Compose Deployment
summary: Write Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, and docker-compose with Postgres and Redis.

sections.content:
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /code

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "4"]

docker build -t myapp .
docker run -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env myapp

FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN uv pip install --system --no-cache -r requirements.txt

FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "4"]

sections.title: Multi-stage benefits
sections.content: Multi-stage builds separate the build environment (with uv, compilers, etc.) from the runtime image. The final image is smaller and has fewer attack surface packages.

services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    command: sh -c "alembic upgrade head && uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4"

  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
      POSTGRES_DB: appdb
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    image: redis:7

volumes:
  pgdata:

sections.title: Key details
sections.content: 1) Postgres healthcheck prevents the app from starting before DB is ready. 2) Migrations run at container start (alembic upgrade head). 3) pgdata volume persists the database across restarts.

items: Use a non-root user in the Dockerfile (add --useradd and USER directive)
Add a healthcheck to the app container
Pin exact versions in requirements.txt (no ranges)
Run behind a reverse proxy (nginx/traefik) for TLS termination

code_challenge.title: Docker-ready FastAPI App
code_challenge.description: Create a minimal FastAPI app suitable for Docker deployment. Add a /health endpoint for container healthchecks.
hints: This endpoint is used by Docker healthchecks to verify the container is running

quiz.question: What does --workers 4 do in the CMD?
options: Runs 4 uvicorn worker processes for concurrency
quiz.explanation: uvicorn --workers 4 spawns 4 worker processes, each running its own event loop. This enables true multi-core utilization.

quiz.question: Why use a multi-stage Docker build?
options: Smaller final image (build tools stay in builder stage only)
quiz.explanation: Multi-stage builds keep build dependencies (compilers, uv) in the builder stage. The final image only copies installed packages, making it smaller and more secure.

quiz.question: What does the Postgres healthcheck do?
options: Checks if the database is encrypted
Prevents the app from starting before the database is ready
quiz.explanation: The healthcheck runs pg_isready. With depends_on: condition: service_healthy, the app waits until the DB is actually accepting connections before starting.

quiz.question: What should be in .dockerignore?
quiz.explanation: Exclude .git (history), __pycache__ (compiled files), .env (secrets!), and tests from the Docker image to reduce size and prevent secret leaks.

quiz.question: Where should TLS termination happen?
quiz.explanation: Use a reverse proxy (nginx, traefik, or a cloud load balancer) for TLS termination. Uvicorn runs behind it handling HTTP, while the proxy handles HTTPS certificates.
